text_blocks.snippet: The top three infectious diseases, often referred to as the "Big Three," are malaria, tuberculosis, and HIV/AIDS. These diseases collectively cause a significant number of deaths and disproportionately affect low- and middle-income countries, according to Global Biodefense.
Here's a bit more detail on each:

list.title: Malaria:
list.snippet: This parasitic disease is transmitted by mosquitoes and can cause flu-like symptoms.

list.title: Tuberculosis:
list.snippet: A bacterial infection that spreads through the air and primarily affects the lungs.

list.title: HIV/AIDS:
list.snippet: This viral disease has caused millions of deaths since its discovery in the 1980s.

text_blocks.snippet: Infectious diseases are illnesses caused by pathogens like bacteria, viruses, fungi, or parasites that can be transmitted from one individual to another or from other sources. Examples include the common cold, influenza (flu), HIV/AIDS, chickenpox, measles, and COVID-19.
snippet_highlighted_words: common cold, influenza (flu), HIV/AIDS, chickenpox, measles, and COVID-19

list.snippet: Viral Infections: Common cold, influenza, HIV/AIDS, chickenpox, measles, COVID-19, Ebola, and Zika virus.
Bacterial Infections: Strep throat, urinary tract infections, tuberculosis, and some forms of pneumonia.
Fungal Infections: Ringworm, athlete's foot, and some lung and brain infections.
Parasitic Infections: Malaria, Chagas disease, and toxocariasis.

list.title: Direct Contact:
list.snippet: Influenza, common cold, HIV/AIDS, chickenpox, and sexually transmitted infections like herpes can be spread through direct contact.

list.title: Airborne Transmission:
list.snippet: Measles, tuberculosis, and influenza can spread through the air when an infected person coughs or sneezes.

list.title: Food or Waterborne:
list.snippet: Salmonella, E. coli, and cholera can be spread through contaminated food or water.

list.title: Vector-Borne:
list.snippet: Malaria and Zika virus are transmitted through mosquito bites.
Hepatitis (A, B, C): Viral infections that can cause liver damage.
Meningitis: Inflammation of the membranes surrounding the brain and spinal cord, which can be caused by bacteria or viruses.
Whooping Cough (Pertussis): A highly contagious respiratory infection.
Norovirus: A common cause of gastroenteritis.
Monkeypox: A viral disease that can cause a rash, fever, and swollen lymph nodes.

text_blocks.snippet: It's important to note that some infectious diseases, like HIV/AIDS, can be treated but not cured, while others, like chickenpox, can be prevented through vaccination.
